These pages hold the materials for two Cushing/Whitney Medical Library classes: **Part 1: Getting started with Claude** and **Part 2: Analyzing research data with Claude Code**.

- **Features last checked:** 2026-10-30
- **Next review due:** `[date]`

## How we keep it current {#review}

Claude and Claude Code change often. Menus get renamed, and features move or depend on your admin's settings.

- We review the site **within 30 days of a major Claude change**, and **at least every 6 months**.
- We check feature claims against the [Claude Help Center](https://support.claude.com) and the [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs).
- Features that depend on Yale's admin settings are marked **(if enabled)**. Local details, such as links, contacts, and approvals, appear in `[square brackets]` until they're confirmed.
- If a page doesn't match what you see in Claude, trust what you see, and [tell us](#report).

## How this site was made {#ai-use}

**AI use:** Drafted with Claude and Claude Code; reviewed by `[instructor]`. Every feature claim was checked against official documentation on the date above.

**Data:** The class files are synthetic (made up) or public. No real patient data is used anywhere on this site. The Kit A article is an open-access paper reused under its Creative Commons license: Hickey MD et al., *PLoS Medicine* 2025, [doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1004632](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1004632). It was reformatted as text for teaching.

**Style:** The look follows the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library web style (CWML web style draft 0.1), applied through a Quarto adapter. Dark mode is a local extension and isn't part of the CWML style. The site's layout borrows from the library's `[All of Us workshop site link]`.

**Built with:** [Quarto](https://quarto.org), published on GitHub Pages.
